 Home Sports NZ vs India | 53/5 in 20 Overs as India Turn Wellington Into a Batting Ordeal NZ vs India | 53/5 in 20 Overs as India Turn Wellington Into a Batting Ordeal
 Open Bureau Last Updated: November 7, 2026, 10:22 IST Summarise Share Share New Zealand added just 24 runs and lost two more wickets between overs 11 and 20 as India extended their grip well beyond the opening spell The opening damage belonged to Auqib Nabi (in pic) and Anshul Kamboj. Nabi removed Tim Seifert for a five-ball duck and Will Young for six from 17 deliveries   Credits: ANI New Zealand had 47 overs available. After using 20 of them, they had managed 53 runs and lost half their batting order.
 Wellington was becoming a prolonged examination of the home side’s batting. Swing and seam had troubled the top order. Then India’s change bowlers extended the discomfort, denying New Zealand the easier passage they desperately needed.

Go Ad-Free At 29/3 after 10 overs, the hosts had already made one of their leanest home ODI starts. The next 10 brought just 24 runs and two more wickets. The scoring rate slipped from 2.9 to 2.65, with New Zealand spending more than two-fifths of their allotted innings trying to find a foothold.

 The opening damage belonged to Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj. Nabi removed Tim Seifert for a five-ball duck and Will Young for six from 17 deliveries. Kamboj bowled Henry Nicholls for 11 from 26.
 Those three innings yielded 17 runs from 48 balls. New Zealand had struggled both to protect their wickets and to score while doing so.
 Recommended Stories NZ vs India | 29/3 in Wellington Brings Back an Uncomfortable 2018 Echo EXPLAINED | ‘Clicky Ponting’ Scandal: How a Finger Snap Fooled a Cricket Umpire "Bharat's Daughter Scripts History": Sports Minister Congratulates Tanvi Patri on Youth Olympics Silver "Second BWF Title of the Season": Kiren Rijiju Congratulates PV Sindhu on HYLO Open 2026 Triumph "We Stuck to Our Plan for 60 Minutes": Harmanpreet After India Clinch Record 6th Asian Champions Trophy Gurnoor Brar then made the middle order’s introduction equally uncomfortable. Tom Latham fell for seven from 22 balls, caught by Naman Dhir. Glenn Phillips lasted four deliveries without scoring before giving Kamboj a catch off Brar.
 Latham and Phillips had used another 26 balls for seven runs. Across the five dismissed batters, New Zealand’s return was 24 runs from 74 deliveries. Almost 12½ overs had been consumed by players who collectively scored at barely two an over.
 That left Daryl Mitchell carrying much of the innings’ scoring burden.
 Boundaries, then long silences
 Mitchell was unbeaten on 24 from 47 deliveries at the 20-over mark. His three fours and a six accounted for 18 runs. The remaining 43 balls he faced produced six.
 The boundary count offered occasional relief. Between those shots, India repeatedly closed the scoring down. Mitchell’s strike rate of 51.06 was still the highest among New Zealand’s six batters to that point.
 For the hosts, this was the more troubling development. The difficult opening had continued into a second block of 10 overs, with fresh batters unable to loosen India’s control.
 Familiar conditions, unfamiliar authority
 New Zealand’s 29/3 after 10 overs had recalled their 28/3 against England in Hamilton in 2018. By the 20th over in Wellington, the more immediate story was India’s ability to sustain that pressure.
 Home conditions had supplied movement. India had supplied successive bowlers capable of exploiting the uncertainty it created. New Zealand’s familiarity with those demands had brought little reward.
 There were still 27 overs available. But at 53/5, the hosts had already lost much of the batting needed to use them aggressively. India’s opening spell had become a 20-over hold on the innings.
